final_message:
` and `report.json` are done. All 27 training instances now give a certified value above the Bernoulli wall. I stopped because a wider search found no further improvement.

**What the strategy does:**

| Part | Rule |
|---|---|
| Two atoms (closed form) | For each j, set a = max(0, (t−j)/(n−j)) and b = (t−(n−j)a)/j. For j = 0, a = t/n and b = 1. Then keep the j with the best binomial tail. For fixed j, the weight q on b increases with a (because nm > t), so a is set as low as possible. |
| Three atoms | Atoms are the vertices of {c·a = t, aᵢ ∈ {0, 1}}. The weights are set by a local search, and the search stops after 3.5 s. |

**Results:**
- 26 of the 27 instances are best with 2 atoms, as the hint said.
- n6_m3-5_t9-10 is better with 3 atoms, {0, 0.9, 1}. The added mass at 1 lifts the mean, and the value goes from 0.017833 to 0.017904 (+7e-5).
- Calls take at most 0.5 s on the training instances and about 3.5 s for n = 12–16.

**What did not help:**
- An exhaustive 4-atom search on n ≤ 4 found nothing better.
- On n = 6, a 4-atom search with atoms at 0 and 1, plus a random sample of 4-atom laws, also found nothing better.
- Nothing here proves that these laws are optimal.

**`report.json` probabilities:**

| Instances | Probability |
|---|---|
| n = 3 | 0.75 |
| n = 4 | 0.70 |
| n = 6 | 0.60 |
| n6_m3-5_t9-10 | 0.45 |

The n = 6 instances get less confidence because those searches were only partial, and n6_m3-5_t9-10 gets the least because it needs a richer law than 2 atoms.
